rejected.title: Multiculturalism
card: Multiculturalism is the idea that people from many cultural backgrounds can live in one country and keep their own cultures and languages. It is also a government policy.

From the late 1940s to the mid-1960s, governments expected migrants to assimilate: to give up their old ways and become like the British-background majority. From the mid-1960s, a policy of integration accepted that migrants might keep some of their culture.
In the 1970s the Whitlam government and then the Fraser government made multiculturalism official policy. Both supported migrants to keep their cultures and languages.
Support included services for migrants, such as interpreters, and programs to share different cultures. One example is the Special Broadcasting Service (SBS), which broadcasts in many languages.
rejected.remember: Multiculturalism backs migrants to keep their cultures and languages, and it became official policy in the 1970s.

a.q: What did the official policy of multiculturalism support migrants to do?
opts: Keep their cultures and languages while living in Australia
Give up their old ways and copy the majority culture
Live apart from other Australians in separate communities
Return to their countries of origin after a few years
a.why: Multiculturalism supported migrants to keep their cultures and languages as part of Australian life. Giving up old ways describes assimilation, the policy from the late 1940s to the mid-1960s.
a.clue: Think about what the earlier policies asked of migrants.

b.q: In 1960, a council officer in Sydney tells a new Greek family to stop speaking Greek in public and to adopt local habits quickly. Which policy idea does this fit best?
opts: Assimilation, the policy until the mid-1960s
Multiculturalism, as adopted by the Whitlam government
Multiculturalism, as adopted by the Fraser government
A policy to support migrants to keep their languages
b.why: The officer expects the family to give up its old ways and become like the majority. That is assimilation, the policy from the late 1940s to the mid-1960s. Multiculturalism came in the 1970s and backed migrants to keep their cultures and languages.
b.clue: Check the date and what the family is told to give up.
